what: The wire contract for a calendar's default reminders — the synced user-pref that TypeScript writes and Rust reads. Both suites read THIS file, so a rename on either side fails a test instead of going silent.
why: The Rust reader ends in serde_json::from_str::<Vec<DefaultReminder>>(raw).unwrap_or_default(). One unparsable entry discards the WHOLE list, with no log line and nothing visible in the UI: the settings panel still shows the reminders (it reads back its own writer), while new appointments reach the provider with no alarm, the in-Aperio overlay stops firing, and every birthday calendar goes quiet because an empty list reads as 'the user cleared it'. Nothing but running the real app on a real account would show it — which is exactly the manual test this file exists to retire.

clearMarker.note: Both clients write an empty STRING to clear the list rather than deleting the key. A deleted key reads as 'never configured', which brings a birthday calendar's built-in reminder straight back — the off switch would turn itself on again. The empty string must therefore decode to an empty list, not to 'unset'.

samples.name: with-a-system-sound

samples.name: absolute

samples.name: empty-list
samples.note: A list the user emptied on purpose. Distinct from a missing key, which means 'never configured'.
